rounds.text: The company’s operating margins are stagnant and inconsistent, failing to show meaningful improvement despite aggressive expansion plans [E24, E26, E27]. While the business is growing, the lack of a dividend payout suggests that capital is being trapped within the firm rather than returned to shareholders, a policy explicitly confirmed by management to conserve resources [E4, E58, E80]. Investors should also note the significant decline in foreign institutional ownership, which has dropped from 8.79% to 4.92% over the last two years [E37]. Furthermore, the stock exhibits high annualised volatility of 48.5% and a negative Sharpe ratio of -0.36, indicating that the risk-adjusted returns have been poor [E49, E50]. The historical record of a -71.5% peak-to-trough drawdown serves as a stark reminder of the potential downside for shareholders [E48]. Conceded: the company has demonstrated strong compounded sales and profit growth [E14, E17], maintains a conservative debt-free balance sheet [E32, E55], and has seen an increase in promoter holdings [E36, E57].
